Every `Core\Test` bench is measured again, because `test.rs` changed.

items.text: **`Core\Test\SentRequest::body`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, tests and the class card for `Core\Test\SentRequest` (add a `ClassDoc` beside `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs:955` and delete the class from `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs:5348`). The row is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs:987` and its card `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs:1542`, which needs the plain voice. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. The Rust test `sent_http_returns_one_record_per_call_in_the_order_they_were_made` reads the body slot directly, so a `covers:` test must call `nvs_core_test_sent_body`. The examples need `Core\Test::answerHttp` so the call is answered from the table, as `benches/members/core/Http-Response/status.nvs` does.

backlog: Indexing an array with a `uint` expression allocates twice per read, and with an `int` it does not; a codegen or runtime cost on the request path. Owner: the playbook bullet under *Writing a test case* until a goal takes it.

A `Core\Test::request` whose program runs out of memory ends the whole test program with a FATAL, because the child's output counts against the test's own memory limit. `rule:testing/in-process-request` does not say whether a test should see `500` there instead.
